_stateTableNote: State and locality tables exist only for 2025 in the source. The 2024 and 2026 engines explicitly piggyback the 2025 state tables — the Dart comment says the state-rate cadence is slower than federal and the difference is generally under 0.1pp. Do not present the 2025 state figures as 2024 or 2026 figures.

2024.note: Statutory § 1(j)(2) rate schedules with the § 63(c) basic standard deduction applied to gross wages. Annual filing liability, not payroll withholding.
2024.bracketSource: Derived from the band widths of the IRS Pub. 15-T (2024) STANDARD Withholding Rate Schedules, ANNUAL payroll period (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/p15t--2024.pdf). The derivation was verified against the § 1(j)(2) rate tables printed in Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.01 for 2026 — exact match on all four filing statuses.

fica.source: IRS Pub. 15 (2024) — social security wage base limit. Rates and Additional Medicare thresholds are statutory.

limits.source: IRS Notice 2023-75 (401(k)); Rev. Proc. 2023-23 (HSA); Rev. Proc. 2023-34 (health FSA)

2025.note: Statutory § 1(j)(2) rate schedules with the OBBBA-amended § 63(c) standard deduction applied to gross wages. The 2025 Pub. 15-T withholding tables were published 2024-12-09, before OBBBA, so payroll withholding in 2025 is based on the pre-OBBBA $15,000 deduction and runs higher than actual liability. This table models liability.
2025.standardDeductionSource: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.08 — OBBBA § 70102 amended § 63(c)(7) retroactively for tax years beginning after 2024-12-31, raising the 2025 basic standard deduction above the $15,000 / $22,500 / $30,000 originally announced in Rev. Proc. 2024-40
2025.bracketSource: Derived from the band widths of the IRS Pub. 15-T (2025) STANDARD Withholding Rate Schedules, ANNUAL payroll period (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/p15t--2025.pdf). The derivation was verified against the § 1(j)(2) rate tables printed in Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.01 for 2026 — exact match on all four filing statuses.

fica.source: IRS Pub. 15 (2025) — social security wage base limit. Rates and Additional Medicare thresholds are statutory.

limits.source: IRS Notice 2024-80 (401(k) elective deferral, age-50 catch-up, SECURE 2.0 age 60-63 catch-up); Rev. Proc. 2024-25 (HSA); Rev. Proc. 2024-40 (health FSA)
